findings.title: Exit code semantics swapped: 4 changes meaning from 'recreate needed' to 'feature disabled'
findings.body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE moved from 4 to 3 and 4 is now reused for FEATURE_DISABLED. Any existing automation/script (or operator logic) that treats exit code 4 as "recreate upgrade required" will now silently interpret a feature-disabled run (where no compatibility check happened at all) as "recreate required", and will not recognize the new code 3. Since both meanings are mutually inconsistent, this is a breaking contract change that should be called out in release/upgrade notes, and ideally the feature-disabled code should be a fresh value rather than the previously used 4.

findings.title: No assertion on exit code for feature-disabled path, and check subcommand not covered
findings.body: testFeatureNotEnabled only asserts the error message for the `metadata` subcommand. The newly introduced exit code (CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED = 4) is the documented contract for scripting, but no test verifies it; likewise the `check` subcommand's feature-disabled behaviour is untested. A regression in the exit code (e.g. the recent 3/4 renumbering) would go unnoticed.
